Sponsored by



Rachel Mendelson/WSJ



Trouble in the bond market is forcing investors to anticipate where the economy—and their portfolios—are headed.

So how will the economy handle rising rates—and what should investors do to prepare?

The Wall Street Journal  asked six leading money managers for their thoughts [https://www.wsj.com/finance/investing/investors-trade-bond-yields-treasuries-60ee83f9].

Below, some of the best analysis and insight from WSJ writers and columnists, the Dow Jones Newswires team and occasionally beyond, on investing, the wealth-management business and more.

Planning & Investing               How to Know When the AI Boom Is About to Go Bust

History shows that market manias end when the  capital spigot turns off [https://www.wsj.com/finance/stocks/how-to-know-when-the-ai-boom-is-about-to-go-bust-61af3d26].

The Surprise Social Security Benefit That Goes to Parents Who Have Kids Late

Social Security recipients can get  an additional benefit [https://www.wsj.com/personal-finance/the-surprise-social-security-benefit-that-goes-to-parents-who-have-kids-late-05497d3e] for dependent children, which alters the calculation about when to draw benefits.

Market Talk               

From  Dow Jones Newswires [https://www.dowjones.com/professional/newswires/]



Analysts project that September's slowdown in payroll growth shouldn't interfere with the Fed's plan to remain focused on inflation. Upcoming revisions to the central bank's preferred measure, PCE will come this Wednesday. "The revisions shouldn't impact the near-term policy path, since the Fed was likely already accounting for them," says an analysis from BofA. Economists polled by The Wall Street Journal expect 83,000 jobs added in September. A note from Oxford Economics projects payroll growth to increase by a lower 50,000, with the biggest swing occurring in leisure and hospitality, suggesting the last report's increase was due to seasonal noise. (Jessica Coacci, jessica.coacci@wsj.com)

The U.K. could announce a relatively small budget on Oct. 28, due to constrained public finances, Aberdeen Investments' Lizzy Galbraith says in a note. The latest U.K. public finances data show public borrowing stood at 18.3 billion pounds in August, 19% higher than in the same period a year ago. "Tough decisions on welfare, youth unemployment, social care and long-term defense spending" could be pushed to 2027's government spending review or announced at the release of Prime Minister Andy Burnham's 10-year plan, Galbraith says. (Miriam Mukuru, miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

Learn More  [http://pubads.g.doubleclick.net/gampad/clk?id=7429927158&iu=/2]

Barron's Advisor               5 Tips to Help Young Adults Avoid the Dreaded ‘Failure to Launch’

Parents and financial advisers can help young people  establish a strong financial game plan [https://www.barrons.com/advisor/articles/financial-advice-20s-77167862] when first leaving home.

Business & Practice               Prada Is Wooing the Ultrarich With Snorkeling Trips and $100,000 Skirts

The fashion house is working to close the gap with rivals in courting top spenders as it navigates  a difficult climate for luxury retail [https://www.wsj.com/business/retail/prada-is-wooing-the-ultrarich-with-snorkeling-trips-and-100-000-skirts-feee7a9f].

Impact Investing               Nevada Is Making Surprising Gains in Solar Energy

The sun beats down 300 days a year in southern Nevada, where energy developers hope a vast desert, dotted with spiky green shrubs known as Spanish daggers, will play host to  a new generation of solar farms [https://www.wsj.com/business/energy-oil/nevada-solar-industry-trump-states-b838c7e4].

Talking Points               These $10,000 Cameras Are a Rare European Manufacturing Success

Leica’s retro designs have survived various crises, but  its playbook [https://www.wsj.com/business/retail/these-10-000-cameras-are-a-rare-european-manufacturing-success-d91cf324] may not work for everyone.

Travel & Lifestyle               Go to Boulder for the Mountains. Stay for the Culture            

Photograph by David Williams for WSJ



The Sundance Film Festival’s move to the small mountain city next year will put it on the cultural map. Insiders know it has  long been a hub for cool creative types [https://www.wsj.com/lifestyle/travel/boulder-colorado-sundance-trip-a1c3194c].
